simple.meaning: יָשַׁט (yâshaṭ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to extend.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Esther, beginning at Esther 4:11. The surrounding contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָשַׁט (H3447) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָשַׁט (yâshaṭ) / H3447 is traced through Esther 4:11, Esther 5:2, Esther 8:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, know, that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”

timeline.evidenceText: “All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, know, that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”

When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. So Esther came near, and touched the top of the scepter.
Then the king held out to Esther the golden scepter. So Esther arose, and stood before the king.
